title: Biggest order
scenario: For each customer, their single biggest order amount.

intro.job: For each customer, their single biggest order amount.

idea.rule: max(orders) looks at the OUTER box — the names. max(orders[name]) opens that customer's box first.
idea.detail: orders is a dict whose values are lists. orders['ana'] opens the outer box and hands you ana's list [5, 12, 7]; one more step — max(...) — reaches into that list. Each pair of brackets opens one more box, so say what's in your hand after each one.

model_restatement: For every customer, find the largest amount in their list of orders.

clarify.question: Could a customer have no orders?
clarify.answer: Not today — everyone has at least one.

clarify.question: What if two orders tie for biggest?
What shape should the answer be?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: For each customer, take the biggest of the orders. Put it in a dict. Print it.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after iteration 1, what is biggest?

why_line: max(orders) is handed the whole dict of customers — and max of a dict looks at its keys, so it picks the biggest NAME, 'ben', not an amount.

explain.rule: max(orders) reaches into the wrong box: it opens the box of customers and picks the biggest name tag — 'ben' — instead of opening ana's box of amounts.
explain.bridge: So which box should max be handed — the box of customers, or ana's box of orders?

fix.rule: max(orders[name]): open the customer's box, then hand the whole list to max.

walk.gloss: An empty dict for the answers.
Open their list of orders and keep the biggest.

alternatives.code: print({name: max(amounts) for name, amounts in orders.items()})

hints: After iteration 1, did ana get an amount — or a name?
max(orders) looks at the dict's keys — the customer names. Open this customer's box first.

follow_up.prompt: One customer, one order: {'cy': [9]} — what's printed?

checkpoint.prompt: With the new orders, what gets printed?

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — max still finds the biggest.

one_liner: max(orders) looks at the OUTER box — the names. max(orders[name]) opens that customer's box first.
